commands.name: install
commands.description: Install dependencies exactly as the lockfile pins them, across the workspaces.

commands.name: build
commands.description: `tsc -b` across the workspaces, then each package's postbuild. This is where typechecking happens — there is deliberately no separate `typecheck` script to keep one answer to 'do the types hold'. It is the first gate because `verify` runs it first and the suite reads built output.

commands.name: test
commands.description: The suite, via the package script rather than a bare `vitest run`, so the runner is whatever the repo says it is.

commands.name: lint
commands.description: ESLint. Blocking because a worker can fix it by editing its own output, which is the line between a gate that teaches and one that nags.

commands.name: pregate
commands.description: The local antagonistic review panel, run against the working tree's diff from main. ADVISORY: it reports findings and blocks nothing, so a REJECT is a conversation and not a verdict. It runs a script that lives OUTSIDE this repository (../capabilities), so it is not versioned with the code it reviews and can break without this file changing. It COSTS REAL MONEY on every run — several model calls per lens — which is why it is a release step named one at a time rather than a gate that fires on every verification. --lens-timeout 480s: the panel warms one lens alone then fans the other four behind it, so worst case is TWO lens deadlines (16 min), not five; preflight adds up to three sequential 60s-bounded setup calls (3 min) and rubric provisioning is bounded by this same lens deadline (8 min) — 3 + 8 + 16 = 27 min, inside the script's own hardcoded 30-minute inner backstop (PREGATE_TIMEOUT_MS default) with real margin. The 40-minute timeoutMs below is deliberately ABOVE that inner bound: the script's own backstop must fire first so it can report which lens hung, and this row's timeoutMs exists only to catch a wedged script the inner backstop itself failed to kill.
